Every element ctml knows, in the order they are registered. Nothing in the markup says whether a
tree is a screen or a hud: these are the same elements either way.

An element is always written with a closing tag, except for the three that hold nothing, where one is
allowed and not needed. Every element takes every [property](/ctml/reference/properties), and the
ones listed under **Own properties** below are the ones that do something on that element in
particular.

## Where every element starts

Before a class list or a hand set style touches it, an element carries these:

- `display: block`
- `position: static`
- `box-sizing: border-box`

The styles that come down the tree are not defaults on the element, since a default on every element
would stop a parent's value ever reaching its children. They are seeded once at the root instead:

- `color: #ffffff`
- `font-size: 16`
- `text-align: left`
- `text-shadow: true`
- `white-space: normal`
- `visibility: visible`

## The root

### `<ctml>`

The root of a tree: html and body in one. It fills the screen it is drawn in, and the text values everything below inherits bottom out here, so a tree always has something to inherit from.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Written | `<ctml>` ... `</ctml>` |
| Holds children | yes |
| Own properties | none |
| Starts with | `width: 100%`, `height: 100%`, `margin: 0`, `padding: 0`, and the inherited values, seeded here |
| Java class | `net.tutla.craftytml.client.ctml.element.CTML` |

```html
<ctml class="w-full h-full bg-slate-900 text-slate-100"></ctml>
```

## Layout

### `<div>`

A plain box, and nothing on top of the common defaults, so it is the one every other element varies from. Reach for it whenever nothing more particular is wanted.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Written | `<div>` ... `</div>` |
| Holds children | yes |
| Own properties | none |
| Starts with | the common defaults only |
| Java class | `net.tutla.craftytml.client.ctml.element.Division` |

```html
<div class="flex flex-col gap-2 p-2"></div>
```

### `<hr>`

A line across the block, drawn as the top border of a box with no height.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Written | `<hr>`, with `</hr>` allowed and not needed |
| Holds children | no |
| Own properties | none |
| Starts with | `display: block`, `height: 0`, `border-top-width: 1`, `margin-top: 4px`, `margin-bottom: 4px` |
| Java class | `net.tutla.craftytml.client.ctml.element.markdown.Rule` |

```html
<hr class="w-full border-slate-700">
```

## Lists

### `<ul>`

A list whose items are marked with a shape. list-disc by default, like html.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Written | `<ul>` ... `</ul>` |
| Holds children | yes |
| Own properties | none |
| Starts with | `display: block`, `list-style-type: disc`, `padding-left: 10px`, `margin-top: 4px`, `margin-bottom: 4px` |
| Java class | `net.tutla.craftytml.client.ctml.element.markdown.list.UnorderedList` |

```html
<ul class="list-disc"></ul>
```

### `<ol>`

A list whose items are numbered. start says what to count from and reversed counts down.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Written | `<ol>` ... `</ol>` |
| Holds children | yes |
| Own properties | `start`, `reversed` |
| Starts with | `display: block`, `list-style-type: decimal`, `padding-left: 10px`, `margin-top: 4px`, `margin-bottom: 4px` |
| Java class | `net.tutla.craftytml.client.ctml.element.markdown.list.OrderedList` |

```html

```

### `<li>`

One item of a list, which draws the marker its list asks for. value sets its number.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Written | `<li>` ... `</li>` |
| Holds children | yes |
| Own properties | `value` |

| Java class | `net.tutla.craftytml.client.ctml.element.markdown.list.ListItem` |


## Pictures

### `<img>`

A picture. src names the texture, and the element comes out the size of that texture unless a width or a height says otherwise; naming one of the two keeps the picture's own shape on the other. object-fit says what happens when the box it ends up in is not the picture's shape.

It holds no children, and like every other element here it is still written with a closing tag.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Written | `<img>`, with `</img>` allowed and not needed |
| Holds children | no |
| Own properties | `src` |
| Starts with | `display: inline-block`, `object-fit: fill` |
| Java class | `net.tutla.craftytml.client.ctml.element.markdown.Img` |

```html
<img src="minecraft:textures/block/stone.png" class="w-5 h-5 rounded-sm"></img>
```

## Input

### `<button>`

Something to press. callback names a function the host put in the dom context, and a press on the button, or enter or space while it has the focus, calls it with a `CTMLCallback` of type INPUT.

The name is one function, which hears about everything that happens to the button and not only the presses, so one that cares which is which asks the callback it is handed. Hovering a button is not pressing it, and a function that acts on everything it is told would have it look as though it were.

It is inline-block and centres its text, which is what a browser's button does, and it is in the tab order without having to say so: pressing it is the only thing it is for, so the keyboard can always reach it.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Written | `<button>` ... `</button>` |
| Holds children | yes |
| Own properties | `callback`, `tabindex` |
| Starts with | `display: inline-block`, `text-align: center` |
| Java class | `net.tutla.craftytml.client.ctml.element.input.Button` |

```html
<button class="px-2 py-1 bg-sky-600 rounded hover:bg-sky-500" callback="sayHi" text="press me"></button>
```
